name: Pilotta
description: Pilotta is a Greek point-trick game of the Jass family, popular in Cyprus. Similar to Belote. 4 players in partnerships. Ace-ten scoring. Ioannis Zapitis published rules; WebPilotta available at gamesfair.com.

overview.description: Pilotta is a Greek point-trick game of the Jass family, popular in Cyprus. Similar to Belote. 4 players in partnerships. Ace-ten scoring. Ioannis Zapitis published rules; WebPilotta available at gamesfair.com.

history.origins: Pilotta is a Greek point-trick game of the Jass family, derived from Belote, and is particularly popular in Cyprus. It is played primarily in Cyprus, especially among younger players who often arrange pilotta meetings in cafés and cafeterias. The Greek counterpart played in Greece is named Vida. Ioannis K. Zapitis published rules in English and created the online version WebPilotta (gamesfair.com).

setup.deck: Jass pack (32 or 52 depending on variant).

rules.objective: Score points for tricks and declarations. Target score (variant).
rules.gameplay: As Belote/Jass: deal, bid or pass for trump, play tricks. Follow suit; trump when void. Ace-ten point values. Marriage declarations. See Ioannis Zapitis rules for full detail.
